prompt:
A full-fidelity desktop website homepage design comp, landscape, shown flat with no browser frame and no device. This is the website of a Christian nonprofit that provides reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost, in the Carolinas. The page's ground is a pale buff-grey salt-glazed stoneware surface with a fine orange-peel texture. Layout, top to bottom:

1. NAVIGATION BAR (thin, full width): at left a text wordmark "Beauty From Ashes" in a dignified serif with "SURGICAL MINISTRY" in small spaced capitals below; centered links "Our Mission", "How We Help", "Stories", "Get Involved", "Contact"; at right a small "EN | ES" switch and a solid cobalt-blue button "Give". A thin hand-brushed cobalt line runs under the bar.

2. HERO (about 60% of the height):
- LEFT 45%: small spaced-capitals eyebrow "A CHRISTIAN SURGICAL MINISTRY · CHARLOTTE & FORT MILL". A large deep iron-brown serif headline over three lines: "Restoring more than what can be seen." A short paragraph: "Reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost, for children and adults whose need exceeds their means. Open to everyone." Two buttons: a solid cobalt-blue button "Ask for help" with a subtly brushed edge, and an iron-brown outlined button "Refer someone".
- RIGHT 55%: the page's single dominant visual, a large hand-thrown Carolina stoneware storage jar photographed in soft natural side light against a plain warm stone backdrop. Its shoulder runs with glossy amber and olive-green wood-ash glaze drips; a loose hand-brushed cobalt-blue stroke decorates its belly. Real ceramic photography, quiet and monumental.

3. VALUES BAND (bottom 30%): small spaced capitals "THEREFORE" above a row of six columns separated by short vertical hand-brushed cobalt strokes. Each column holds a serif heading and one line of small sans text: "We Listen." / "We give every patient the time their story deserves." — "We Protect." / "We hold patient safety as our highest surgical standard." — "We Pray." / "We pray with every patient who welcomes it." — "We Accompany." / "We walk with every patient long after surgery ends." — "We Honor." / "We honor the sacrifice behind every patient's decision." — "We Serve." / "We extend surgical care where need exceeds means."

Overall: calm, dignified, professional, warm and hopeful; unmistakably a real nonprofit website with crisp, legible web typography. Not a church bulletin, not a cosmetic surgery advertisement, not a rustic boutique.
